name: New South Wales
summary: A British blue ensign with the state badge in the fly: a red St George's Cross on white, with a gold lion in the centre and a gold eight-pointed star on each arm.
origin: New South Wales, the oldest Australian colony, adopted its badge in 1876, designed by the colonial architect James Barnet and Captain Francis Hixson. It became a state on federation in 1901.

symbols.name: Lion passant guardant
symbols.description: A gold lion at the centre of the cross.

symbols.name: Four stars
symbols.description: Gold eight-pointed stars on the arms of the cross.

history.label: Colony and State of New South Wales

facts: The badge is sometimes called the 'Cross of St George with the Lion of England'.
clues: A blue ensign with a red cross on white, with a gold lion and four gold stars.
The flag of the oldest Australian colony.
Its four stars represent the Southern Cross.
